summary: Walther Wüst (1901–1993) was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD from the University of Munich (1920–1923). He later served there as außerplanmäßiger Professor (1932) and Dean of the Philosophical Faculty (1935–1945), among other institutional leadership roles.

Wannaporn Rienjang is a scholar of archaeology, history, and Buddhist studies who completed her PhD at the University of Cambridge. She served as a British Museum research assistant, Oxford project assistant (attested 2019–2022), and Thammasat University lecturer (attested 2022–2023).

Warren Crawford Cowgill (1929–1985) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Stanford University (~1948–1952) and earned his Ph.D. at Yale University (~1952–1957), where he was appointed professor of linguistics in 1956.

Warren Lee Todd is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Lancaster University under the doctoral supervision of Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad, and also studied under Irina Kuznetsova, Peter Harvey, and Chogye Trichen Rinpoche.

Warrin Ratanamalai is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2007) under the MA supervision of Phra Suthithammanuwat and Phra Srisitthimuni, having also studied under Phra Sudhivorayan and Somjin Sammāpañño.

Waso Harada is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Ryukoku and Koyasan universities. Harada held posts at Koyasan University (attested 1992), Ryukoku University (attested 1999–2006), and Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 2002–2007).
Watari Yanai (1875–1926) was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1900 to 1903 and later held a post there from ~1919 to 1926.

Wataru Ryose is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1987 under doctoral supervisor Minoru Kiyota. Ryose also studied under Genjun Sasaki and Frances Wilson.

Wayne Chandira is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. As of 2026, he is a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University, studying under doctoral supervisor Mark Rowe.

Wayne Proudfoot (1939–) is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned a Master of Theology and a PhD from Harvard. He taught at Fordham University (~1969–1972) and served as Professor of Religion at Columbia University (~1972–2017).

Wei Lin, a scholar of history, archaeology, sinology, and Buddhist studies, studied at Nanjing and Peking Universities and earned a PhD from Ohio State University. Lin worked as an archaeologist at Nanjing Municipal Museum and held several US university teaching posts.

Wei Wu (1949–) is a scholar of Buddhist studies who founded the International Buddhist College. As attested in 2026, Wu serves as Associate Professor and Director of Undergraduate Studies at Emory University.

Wei-Cheng Lin is a scholar of history, archaeology, sinology, and Buddhist studies. Lin served as a professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill until 2015, joining the faculty of the University of Chicago in 2015.

Wei-jen Teng specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies, earning a PhD from Harvard. Teng has taught at Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts and serves as Professor and Dean of Buddhist Studies at Chung-Hwa Institute (attested 2026).

Wei-ming Tu (1940–) is a philosopher and sinologist who earned his Ph.D. at Harvard (~1962–1968). He held posts at Princeton, UC Berkeley, and Harvard (1999–2010), and directed the Harvard-Yenching Institute (1996–2008).

Weijue Shi (1928–2016) was a Buddhist studies figure who ordained and studied under Lingyuan/Linyuan in 1963. He founded Lin Quan Temple (1987), Chung Tai Buddhist Institute (1993), and Chung Tai Shan.
Weirong Shen (1962–) is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. Shen taught at the University of Hong Kong (~2004–2005) and held a post at Renmin University of China (~2006–2016).
Weiru Guan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University, where Yongdong Shi served as MA supervisor (attested 2011).

Weizhong Huang (1969–) is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He held a post at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2012) and serves as a professor at Renmin University of China (attested 2026).

Weldon South Coblin (1944–) is a scholar of sinology, Tibetology, and linguistics. He studied under Fang-Kuei Li (~1968–1972) and had a career at the University of Iowa (~1973–2013), where he is Professor Emeritus of Chinese.
